contexts.text: The house of Aaron = good of love. AC 9806:3. Illustrated. AE 696:19.
The Levites were given to Aaron because Aaron = the Lord as to the priesthood, that is, as to Divine Love. AC 3858:9. AC 3858:11. AC 5307:2.
Aaron at heart worshipped an Egyptian idol. AC 9806:end, AC 10401.
Aaron = the law Divine as to truth; Moses, as to good.

Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? = doctrine of what is good and true. For Aaron represents the Lord as to Divine good or the priesthood; here, however, before he had been initiated into the priesthood, he is the doctrine of what is good and true, wherefore it is said that he was for a mouth to Moses, and Moses was for a god to him. For by Moses is represented the Lord as to Divine truth that proceeds immediately from Him; hence by Aaron [is represented]. Divine truth that proceeds mediately from the Lord, which truth is the doctrine of what is good and true. The truth that Moses here represents is that which cannot be heard or perceived by man, but the truth that Aaron represents is that which can be heard and perceived by man. Hence Aaron is called the mouth, and Moses his god. Hence also Aaron is called the Levite, for Levite = the church's doctrine of what is good and true, which ministers to and serves the priesthood. AC 7009. AC 7270:2.
And Jehovah said to Aaron = the truth of doctrine, and perception therein from the Divine.
And Moses told Aaron = influx of truth that proceeds immediately from the Lord's Divine into truth that proceeds mediately.
And Aaron spake all the words that Jehovah spake to Moses = doctrine thence from the Divine.

And afterwards came Moses and Aaron = the Divine law and doctrine thence... By the Divine law that Moses represents is understood the Word such as it is in its inward sense, thus such as it is in the Heavens; but by doctrine is understood the Word such as it is in its literal sense, thus such as it is on earth. Explained.

Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, draw away the people from their works? = that their Divine law and doctrine will not release them from troubles. Moses = the Lord as to Divine law, and Aaron = the Lord as to doctrine thence.
Aaron and his families represent those things that belong to doctrine.
And Jehovah spake to Moses and to Aaron = instruction anew from the law Divine and at the same time from doctrine.
Aaron took to himself Elisheba... for a woman = doctrine of the Church, and how good and truth are therein conjoined.
Aaron = what is outward of the Spiritual Church, and Moses, what is inward. Explained.
This Moses and Aaron = that this was from the law, that is from the Divine, and from doctrine thence.
And Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet = doctrine thence, (i.e., from the law Divine.) AC 7270.
And Aaron [was] a son of three and eighty years = the state and quality of doctrine.

Say to Aaron = influx of inward law into outward law. The doctrine of what is good and true that Aaron represents is nothing but outward law existing from inward law, that is, through inward law from the Divine.
Inward law that Moses represents is truth accommodated to Angels, and outward law, that Aaron represents is truth accommodated to men. Explained.
And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron = presence of law Divine... Moses represents inward, and Aaron outward law.
And Jehovah said to Moses and to Aaron = instruction anew... Truth that proceeds from Jehovah is represented by Moses and Aaron, inward truth by Moses, and outward by Aaron. AC 7656.
And Moses and Aaron returned unto Pharaoh = presence of truth Divine thence.
Jehovah said to Moses and Aaron = information through truth Divine... Moses represents truth proceeding from the Divine immediately; Aaron, mediately.

(They murmured) against Moses and against Aaron = [against] truth Divine. Moses represents truth Divine proceeding from the Lord immediately, thus inward; and Aaron, truth from the Lord proceeding mediately, thus outward.
And Moses said unto Aaron = influx of truth Divine proceeding immediately from the Lord through truth Divine that [proceeds] mediately. AC 8529.
Aaron spake to all the company of Israel = instruction from the Divine through influx, (i.e.) from the Divine through truth proceeding from the Lord mediately, which is represented by Aaron.
In the inward historical sense, Moses and Aaron do not represent truth Divine, but the religiosity of that nation whose leaders and heads they were.

Moses, Aaron, and Hur = Divine truths in successive order. Moses = Divine truth proceeding immediately; Aaron, Divine truth proceeding mediately; and Hur, Divine truth proceeding mediately through that again.
And Aaron came and all the elders of Israel = things of the church that are primary. Aaron represents truth of doctrine.
They who are intermediate between the celestial and spiritual kingdoms were represented by Moses and Aaron, who were permitted to go up the mountain.
Come up thou and Aaron = conjunction with truth from the Divine, inward and outward.
Aaron and his sons, who filled the office of the high-priesthood, represent the Lord.

Thou and Aaron = the Word in the inward and outward sense. Moses represents the Word; and when Aaron, who was his brother, is joined to him, Moses then represents the Word in the inward sense, and Aaron in the outward.
And there went up Moses and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu = the Word in the inward and outward sense, and doctrine from both.

Behold Aaron and Hur with ye (the elders) = doctrine of truth from such a Word. Aaron here represents doctrine of truth from the outward sense of the Word alone, because, by the elders, over whom Aaron was set as a head below the mountain, were signified those who are in the outward sense of the Word.

The doctrine here represented by Aaron and Hur, being from the outward sense of the Word alone, without the inward sense, was merely idolatrous; wherefore it is said of Aaron, by whom such doctrine was represented, that he made an idol, or golden calf.
By Aaron as high-priest was represented the Lord as to good of love; and by his garments, especially by the ephod, was represented truth of faith that is from good of love.

That man is heard and his worship received when he has been cleansed from evils, was represented by Aaron's not entering into the holy place within the veil until he had expiated himself and the people.
The priestly office that Aaron filled, represents the Lord as to Divine good.
The process of the glorification of the Lord's Human even to Divine good, is described in the inward sense, and was exhibited before the Angels, when Aaron went through these [initiatory rites].
After these had been gone through, Aaron represented the Lord as to Divine good.
Aaron and his sons shall set it in order = perpetual influx from the Lord... By Aaron was represented the Lord as to Divine good, and by his sons, as to Divine truth. AC 10000. AE 502:4.

And thou, make to draw nigh unto thee Aaron thy brother = conjunction of Divine truth with Divine good in the Lord's Divine Human. Moses... represents the Lord as to Divine truth, ... Aaron, as to Divine good.
Aaron was chosen to fill the priestly office because he was the brother of Moses, for thus there was simultaneously represented the brotherhood of Divine truth and also of Divine good in Heaven.
Aaron = a representative of the Lord as to the Divine Celestial, ... which is the Divine of the Lord in the inmost Heaven.
Sons of Aaron = the things that proceed from the Divine Celestial.
And Aaron shall carry the names of the sons of Israel = the preservation by the Lord of good and truth as to every quality... Aaron represents the Lord as to Divine good.
And it shall be upon Aaron = a representative of the Lord. Aaron here represents the Lord as to those things that concern evangelization and worship.
By Aaron was represented the Lord, and by his office, all the work of salvation; and on man's part, worship.
And it shall be upon the forehead of Aaron = from the Divine love of the Lord. Aaron represents the Lord as to Divine good, which is the good of his Divine love.

And Aaron shall carry the iniquity of the holy ones = removal thereby (i.e. by the Divine love) of falsities and evils with those who are in good from the Lord. Aaron represents the Lord as to good of love.
And it shall be upon the forehead of Aaron constantly = a representative of the Lord's love for ever... Aaron represents the Lord.

For the sons of Aaron = Divine truths proceeding from the Divine good of the Lord in the Heavens. It is said in the Heavens, because it is the Divine of the Lord in the Heavens that was represented by the priestly office of Aaron and his sons; Divine good in the Heavens, by the priestly office of Aaron, and Divine truth from Divine good there, by that of his sons. Explained.

And thou shalt put them on Aaron thy brother = such a state of Divine good in the spiritual kingdom... By Aaron was represented the Lord as to Divine good, thus also Divine good that is from the Lord; and by his garments, the Lord's spiritual kingdom joined to His celestial kingdom.

Aaron in his garments represented the Lord as to Divine good in the Heavens, Aaron himself, the Lord as to the Divine celestial there, and his garments, as to the Divine spiritual there, proceeding from the Divine celestial. AC 10067.
In the inward sense of this chapter the glorification of the Lord as to the Human is treated of, which is signified by the inauguration of Aaron and his sons into the priestly office.

The priestly office that is represented by Aaron is the work of the salvation of those who are in the Lord's celestial kingdom, ... but the priestly office represented by the sons of Aaron is the work of the salvation of those who are in the Lord's spiritual kingdom most closely proceeding from His celestial kingdom. AC 10017:2.

And thou shalt sprinkle upon Aaron, and upon his garments = reciprocal unition of Divine good and Divine truth in the higher Heavens. Aaron represents the Lord as to Divine good, which is the Divine good of the Lord in the celestial kingdom, or, what is the same, in the higher Heavens; and the garments of Aaron are a representative of the Lord's spiritual kingdom joined to His celestial kingdom.

And thou shalt put all things upon the palms of Aaron, and upon the palms of his sons = acknowledgement in the Heavens that those things are of the Lord and from the Lord... Aaron and his sons represent the Lord as to Divine good and Divine truth thence proceeding.

And thou shalt do to Aaron and to his sons thus = this representative of the Lord's glorification, and His influx into the Heavens and into the Church. Aaron represents the Lord as to Divine good, and his sons, the Lord as to Divine good spiritual.

And Aaron shall [burn] incense upon it = the elevation by the Lord of worship that is from love and charity... Aaron as high-priest represents the Lord as to Divine good, and as to the work of salvation. AC 10202.

And Aaron and his sons shall wash out of it = a representative of the purification and regeneration of man by the Lord... Aaron represents the Lord as to Divine good celestial, and the sons of Aaron, the Lord as to Divine good spiritual. AC 10278.

Since the Lord is understood by Aaron in a representative sense, therefore by the seed of Aaron are specifically understood those who are in the Lord's Celestial Kingdom, and also by their generations, those who are in His Spiritual Kingdom.
And thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons = inauguration to represent the Lord in both kingdoms.

And the people was gathered together to Aaron = that it betook itself to the outward things of the Word, of the Church and of worship, separated from what is inward... The reason why this is here represented by Aaron, is that he was the head of that nation in the absence of Moses. Explained in AC 10401.
And Moses said to Aaron = perception from what is internal about such an external.
Because Aaron had made it (the people) dissolute = that this [will be done] by the outward things that they will love... Aaron represents what is outward. AC 10512.
And Aaron and all the sons of Israel saw Moses = the perception of those who are in the outward things of the Church, of worship and of the Word, without inward things.
And Aaron and all the princes in the assembly turned back to him = the principal ones who are in outward things, and yet might represent inward things.
In the Word in Heaven for Aaron there is priesthood, and for David, royalty, both of the Lord.
Why a bridegroom there is dressed like Aaron.
